A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DisWM and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes Supplementary Material A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original DMC and MuJoCo Pusher experiments, representation traversals, ablations and sensitivity analyses in Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark results, runtime measurements, latent-dimension sensitivity and sample-diversity analysis in its supplement.

M1.justification: The pretraining, latent distillation and online adaptation procedures, Equations (1)–(5), and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Supplement B documents the previously stated DreamerV2-style behavior learning rather than establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained color-distracted DMC and Pusher coverage, v2 adds Walker Walk → Humanoid Walk and Finger Spin → DrawerWorld DrawerClose/DrawerOpen. DrawerWorld introduces manipulation under changing training textures and an unseen evaluation texture, substantially broadening the evaluated tasks and conditions.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains its original comparator set. Table A adds evaluated comparisons with DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and ContextWM, including the retained Reacher Easy → Cheetah Run task; Table B evaluates TD-MPC2 and ContextWM on DrawerWorld. ContextWM's underlying work was previously discussed as IPV but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include grid-to-wood training with held-out metal-texture evaluation and success-rate measurement, a latent-dimension sweep over 5/10/20/100, and t-SNE analysis of 200 clips of length 50. Table C introduces runtime comparisons at stated 100k/200k training budgets. The retained main DMC settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds texture-shift robustness evaluation, latent-dimension sensitivity (Figure I), offline/online sample-diversity visualization (Figure J), and runtime/model-size analysis (Table C). Figure 8 extends the existing video-source analysis with Hopper Stand. The original component ablations and weight-sensitivity results remain.

E5.justification: v1 presents shaded learning-curve bands; v2 additionally reports explicit numerical ± spreads in Tables A–B. Neither version defines the uncertainty measure or reports seeds/run counts. This is a limited reporting addition, not evidence that repetitions increased.

E6.justification: New results include DisWM episode returns of 817 ± 59 on Cheetah Run and 147 ± 85 on Humanoid Walk in Table A, and DrawerClose/Open success rates of 77 ± 6% and 70 ± 10% in Table B. Table C and Figures I–J add further outcomes. Figure 8 gains a source condition; TED's curve/band in Figure 4(e) and the Finger Spin traversal example in Figure 5 are revised.

T1.justification: Supplement B newly supplies formal actor/critic objectives and the recursive λ-return definition in Equations (6)–(9). The existing POMDP formulation and Equations (1)–(5) remain unchanged, and no theorem, proof or formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about transferring disentanglement knowledge from distracting videos to improve downstream control. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: Supplement C.3 newly explains poorer performance at small latent dimensions as impaired disentangled representation learning. The interpretation that online adaptation enriches sample diversity and the limitation concerning complex, time-varying background distractions were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 fills substantial disclosure gaps through Supplement B's MLP/ELU and behavior-learning details and Table D's loss scales, learning rates, batch settings, imagination horizon and return parameters. Table C adds resource profiles. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to retained experimental settings; the project link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting TD-MPC2, DrawerWorld/MetaWorld, ELU, t-SNE and additional visual-RL generalization work, while removing the Distracting Control Suite citation and associated inspiration statement. It also revises the description of Dunion et al. The main positioning relative to APV, IPV and PreLAR remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology, affiliation and acknowledgement edits, moves baseline descriptions from Section 4.1 to Supplement A, and adds supplementary cross-references. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn with clearer Gaussian and action-conditioning annotations. Figure 8 is relocated and its legend extended, and Figure 5 replaces the Finger Spin strip. New performance, runtime and hyperparameter tables plus sensitivity and t-SNE plots substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence beyond color distractions and missing training disclosures. Held-out texture evaluation, harder control tasks and stronger-baseline comparisons broaden the empirical support, while Supplements B and D make the procedure more reproducible. Undefined ± values, absent run counts and unequal runtime budgets still limit interpretation, but the gains in evidential coverage and technical transparency are substantial.
